requirements.evidence: Migration database/migrations/2026_10_29_062759_create_entity_invites_table.php:15-27 has entity_id cascade FK, nullable invited_by, email, role default employee, expires_at, accepted_at, timestamps and unique(entity_id,email); app/Models/EntityInvite.php:38 normalizes e-mail in the mutator and :53 defines pending; app/Actions/InviteMember.php:29-71 authorizes, rejects member/pending on inviteEmail, catches UniqueConstraintViolationException, expires in 7 days, queues the mail and audits; app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:63-101 validates inviteEmail/inviteRole, only hits the 10/hour limiter on success and resets; app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:19-34 accepts (invitee-only, expired -> 'invite', accepted no-op, membership, tenant session, redirect) and :40 declines; resources/views/livewire/entity/pending-invites.blade.php:5-7 emits <hr> and ui.invites_title only when invites exist; resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:149 exact modal header, :163 role select without empty option; app/Mail/EntityInviteMail.php:28-38 subject/queued markdown view.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through app/Actions/{InviteMember,AcceptInvite,DeclineInvite,CancelInvite}.php; authorization via app/Policies/EntityInvitePolicy.php; generated-style migration with reversible down(); #[Fillable] attribute; docs/CHANGELOG updated (CHANGELOG.md:9,17,18, docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md); Bulma markup and {{ }} escaping used throughout. Deviations: app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:140 validates memberRole with inline rules instead of a #[Validate] attribute like the sibling properties, and Members.php:182 cancelRemoval() does not authorize.

security.evidence: app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:55 and :65 authorize 'update' on the locked entity; every membership/invite argument is re-resolved through $this->entity->...->findOrFail (Members.php:112,124,134,190) so client IDs cannot cross entities; app/Actions/InviteMember.php:31, AcceptInvite.php:23, DeclineInvite, CancelInvite authorize through the policy; app/Policies/EntityInvitePolicy.php:15-41 restricts accept/decline to the normalized e-mail match and cancel to owner/admin; public input properties carry rules and are validated; rate limiter at Members.php:75/98; all Blade output uses {{ }}.

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage: tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php (access 403, invite validation/duplicates/expiry, quota, cancel, modal, saveRole owner/last-manager, removal), InviteActionsTest.php (authorization, race, replacement, accept idempotency), PendingInvitesTest.php (tamper, expired, no-op, 404), InvitesOnPagesTest.php (onboarding <hr> and switcher), EntityInviteModelTest.php, EntityInviteSchemaTest.php, EntityInviteMailTest.php, SettingsTest.php. Gap: MembersTest 'employees cannot send, cancel or change anything' only asserts the mount is forbidden, so sendInvite/saveRole/confirmRemoval/openMember have no per-action unauthorized-call test as the conventions require.

simplicity.evidence: Small focused action classes and reuse of existing policy/scopes; but authorization is duplicated on every path (Members.php:65 + InviteMember.php:31, PendingInvites.php:23 + AcceptInvite.php:23) and the accepted-invite idempotency check exists in both PendingInvites.php:26 and AcceptInvite.php:41, adding avoidable duplication.

readability.evidence: Clear class/method names, PHPDoc on new classes and public methods (e.g. Members.php:26-29, InviteMember.php:18-28, EntityInvite.php:15-21), methods stay small, Blade modal markup is consistent and accessible (role=dialog/alertdialog, aria-modal, labels).

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: feature code, mail view, lang keys, tests, and docs/tests updates; the Settings.php:84 invite cleanup and the default-page.blade.php:44 manager-only nav plus dashboard.blade.php manager-only button are direct consequences of the manager-only members page.

issues.explanation: memberRole is validated with inline rules in saveRole() instead of a #[Validate] attribute on the public property, unlike the sibling inviteEmail/inviteRole properties and the project's stated Livewire validation pattern.

cancelRemoval() is a public Livewire action without any $this->authorize(...) call, so it is the one action that does not follow the 'authorize every action' rule; impact is nil because it only clears a UI flag.

issues.location: tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php ('employees cannot send, cancel or change anything')
issues.explanation: The unauthorized-call test only proves that mounting the component is forbidden and never exercises sendInvite, saveRole, confirmRemoval or openMember as an employee, while the Livewire security policy asks for an unauthorized test per action.
The pt_BR copy renders "Você foi convidado(a) para :entity" whereas the task quotes "Você foi convidado..."; the added "(a)" is a small wording deviation from the specified text.

issues.location: app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:65 with app/Actions/InviteMember.php:31 (also PendingInvites.php:23 with AcceptInvite.php:23)
issues.explanation: Every invite/accept/cancel path authorizes twice (component plus action class), which is harmless defense-in-depth but duplicates the policy call.

review.summary: The change replaces instant member addition with a full invite flow: a new entity_invites table/model/policy, four action classes, a queued markdown invite mail, a PendingInvites component on onboarding and the switcher, and a manager-only members page with invite list, member detail modal and removal confirmation. It covers the task and contract and is security-conscious, with extensive Pest coverage. The overall score is 4 because of a few nits: inline memberRole rules instead of #[Validate], an unauthorized cancelRemoval action, and per-action unauthorized tests limited to the component mount.
